text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Young Democrat MP Tamas Deutsch demanded a stringent examination into the matter of the huge payments by the State Privatisation and Holding Co. to a solicitor whose task is to bargain with local governments regarding their compensation.
- Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman announced a restructuring plan for his ministry reducing its staff to 540 from 640.

- Romanian President Iliescu and Prime Minister Nicolae Vacaroiu will travel to Budapest at an unspecified date in the future to issue a "political communique" and sign a document, said Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szent-Ivanyi.

- More than half of the companies in the simplified privatisation programme were sold in its first year for an aggregate HUF 4.5 billion, said Imre Ragats, executive director of the State Privatisation and Holding Co.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Deputy Prime Minister Gabor Kuncze said in Parliament it is "unfortunate" that some of the changes made to the basic treaty between Hungary and Romania "can, after all, be interpreted ... as if they went beyond simple stylistic changes". (Kuncze, also the Interior Minister, is filling in for Prime Minister Gyula Horn, who has the flu.)
- All six parliamentary parties submitted their recommendations on modifying the draft Constitution by Tuesday's deadline.

- Despite the fact that Hungary is a smaller market than either Poland or the Czech Republic, it continues to be the number one East European country to invest in, the German paper Handelsblatt reported in its Tuesday edition.
- Polgari Bank will no longer act as the custodian bank of the fund manager Pannonia's two funds as of March 19, 1997. This is the first time a Hungarian bank has cancelled such an agreement.
- The Defence Forces has lifted the moratorium imposed on flights of MIG-21s.
- The first large-scale conference of Hungarian non-profit organisations, entitled Nonprofit Expo '96, will take place September 27-28 in Budapest.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Three times the average level of rain has fallen on Hungary since mid-August, spelling trouble for the farming sector.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- In an answer to a question regarding the secret clause in the privatisation contract of Budapest Bank, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said in Parliament that he is ready to make public the clause but agreement of the bank's buyers, GE Capital and the EBRD, would be required.
- The success of the next phase of MOL's privatisation may be endangered by the increasing Russian presence of Gazprom in Hungary, the British news agency Reuter quotes Nomura Securities Research.
- Analysts estimate that the annual profit of the national telecoms company Matav may rise 20 per cent in real terms in the next five years.
- The Hungarian Investment and Development Bank and its subsidiaries will operate as a bank group from next year.
- The Central European International Bank has taken out a $150 million syndicated loan from a consortium of 15 international banks.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
